units.translation: With the words ἀνθρωποειδὲς θηρίον ὕδατι συζῶν [a human-shaped beast living in water] the grammarian interpreted the poet's words which had fallen out of the lemma in Phrynichus, and these seem to have been approximately: ἀνθρωπόμορφον κῆτος ἐξ ἁλὸς φανέν [a human-shaped sea-monster appearing from the sea]. I have discussed this at greater length in Philologus vol. 12 p. 189 and 17 p. 720, comparing the verse which Plutarch cites from Euripides, Mor. p. 22: κήτος θοάζον ἐξ Ἀτλαντικής ἁλός [a sea-monster speeding from the Atlantic sea], which we know was taken from the Andromeda from the scholium on Euripides Orest. 335, edited by me, vol. 2 p. 111, 22 of the Oxford edition, where the words κῆτος θοάζον [a sea-monster speeding] are quoted from the Andromeda.
A human-shaped beast living in water: [said] of Glaucus appearing from the sea. Aeschylus (fr. 24).
a human-shaped beast living in water
a human-shaped sea-monster appearing from the sea
a sea-monster speeding from the Atlantic sea
where Hermann probably corrected to καὶ παῖς νεογνὸς ἂν μάθοι [even a newborn child would learn]
[τἀνθρώπων [the affairs of humans] corrupt in fr. 98.]
But his boast is not in accordance with a human.
Such a great number of people.
I fear that my great source of wealth may become for humans a plunder of the one who got there first.
In time, fear fades for humans.
Dearest to his father of all humans.
With whom neither any god nor any human mingles.
The lots that are among humans.
Among the immortals and those under the earth and among humans.
even a newborn child would learn
[erroneously for ἀναδῦν [to emerge]. See ἀναδύομαι [to rise up].]
Breathing from his mind an impious, turning, unclean, unholy [spirit].
And the daimon, unconquerable, unwarlike, unholy.
Hades (more probably Aidoneus) as sender-up may you send up (thus Brunck for ἂν εἴη [would be]) Hades, the divine lord of the Darians.
O Earth, send up my father for me to watch the battle.
The earth, stained with the pollutions of ancient blood, sent them up.
Do not — send up under pain black foam from humans.
From the sown men — a root is sent up.
where perhaps in both places κακά [evils] should be added, as in v. 256.
You have brought upon me much-remembered blood that cannot be washed away.
[Suppl. 323 wrongly M Ἀργεῖον ἀνστήσας στόλον [having raised the Argive expedition], but in the margin ἀντήσας [having met].]
(with aorist ἀνέστην [I stood up] and future ἀναστήσομαι [I will stand up])
